description: UTF-16 key-order fork, minimal pair. U+1F600 GRINNING FACE (UTF-16 D83D DE00) vs U+FB33 HEBREW LETTER DALET WITH DAGESH (UTF-16 FB33). RFC 8785 section 3.2.3 sorts member names on UTF-16 code units: the emoji sorts FIRST (D83D < FB33) although its code point is higher (U+1F600 > U+FB33). Every prior corpus name is BMP, where the two orders coincide, so no earlier vector can distinguish a code-point-sorting implementation from a conforming one.
note: A code-point-sorting implementation emits the members in the reverse order, pre-image bytes 7b22efacb3223a322c22f09f9880223a317d, digest 96c4e1b26f2ef1f5f03e115d3128f9306830bf5eaf2d523c0f7551d3424e4937 -- exactly the UTF-32 order RFC 8785 section 3.2.3 names as incompatible. No member is null, an empty array, or an empty object, so jcs-n normalization is the identity and the same digest serves jcs-s.
